solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The Parisian is after Penny with exceptional piece of cake

indicators.note: the French article is placed after the other pieces, at the end

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for an old British penny (from Latin denarius)
something exceptional is odd, out of the ordinary
le is the French word for 'the', as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's slice of cake follows a penny and something odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of cake' reads as food but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British expressions for a task that is very easy to do.

clue.text: Wally the pickpocket succeeded with credit

parts.note: dip is slang for a pickpocket
S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: A fool of a pickpocket got away with things on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: A wally is British slang for a foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang insults for a silly, stupid person.

clue.text: Nothing girl put in hollow hides smell

indicators.note: the nought and the girl's name are placed inside the word for a hollow

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow in a surface
O looks like zero, nothing
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl with nothing is sent into a hole that conceals a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A body spray or stick is applied precisely to mask unpleasant odour.

definitions.meaning: a German art song for voice and piano, as by Schubert

explanation.surface: Someone garbled the words of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a German word, plural Lieder, used in English for classical songs.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is past tense of telling falsehoods; the noun is a classical German art song.

clue.text: Stands at the game to see Queen in shadows

indicators.note: the Queen's letters are placed within the word for shadows

parts.note: traces and shadows both mean faint signs or remnants
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Fans in the stands at a match spot the Queen in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: These are the stepped standing areas at British football grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered banks of steps where spectators stand to watch football are the ground's stands.

indicators.note: the rodent is discovered inside the comedian's first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, of Morecambe and Wise
a rat is a typical example of vermin

explanation.surface: Rats are turning up at random in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire town, but it gives the comedian's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe behaviour that is irregular and cannot be foreseen.

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, gives the engineer; the 's is read as 'has'
traction is the act of drawing or pulling a load

explanation.surface: An engineer withdraws a technical drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' looks like a plan on paper, but means pulling, as in traction.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawing a statement or claim one has made is a synonym for taking it back.

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
to have met someone is to have come across them

explanation.surface: A military officer bumped into an astronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy body orbiting the sun travels through space, a whimsical description.

definitions.note: read as 'Parody is', so the definition is the word parody

parts.note: a committee that met is said to have sat
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: A lampoon is received with fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are forms of mocking imitation that ridicule their target through exaggeration.

clue.text: Son removed small piles of corn

parts.note: took, as in took away, means removed
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A son has cleared away little heaps of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' reads as describing the piles, but gives just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: These are groups of sheaves of cut grain stood upright in a field to dry.

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A news report has been prepared about a dissident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal, turning REPORTSET around.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident publicly objects to authority, exactly what a demonstrator does.

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

explanation.surface: An office temp is given time to charm someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to lure or entice someone into doing something.

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: A left-winger watches the Conservative leader and dismisses it all as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tory leader' reads as a politician but is just the first letter of Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword staple: short informal word for a Trotskyist, a type of revolutionary communist.

clue.text: Bill arrests staff of delivery supervisor

indicators.note: to arrest is to catch and hold, so the notice holds the pole inside it

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice or poster
a staff is a pole, as is a mast

explanation.surface: A policeman called Bill arrests the staff of a delivery boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a name or a police officer, but means a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The official in charge of a post office oversees the delivery of mail.

indicators.note: a corrupted text has its letters spoiled and jumbled

explanation.surface: A wicked lesson has spoiled someone's good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns describe the quality of being pleasing and attractive to look at.

clue.text: Officer is eating meat of antelope

indicators.note: the officer takes the meat inside, as if eating it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
ham is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: An officer is dining on antelope meat.
explanation.definitionFit: This goat-like mountain animal of Europe is classed as a goat antelope.

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A German is caught with new fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft fabric woven from plant fibre is a common textile.

indicators.note: the choosing word hides the period inside it

parts.note: opting means choosing
an era is an age, a period of history

explanation.surface: Someone prefers to keep their age a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' at the start looks like a link, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is on is running, functioning, in action.

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Take the dogs on a lead around a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth or base supporting a statue is a short pillar, a column.

indicators.note: the word for formerly sits inside the motoring club's letters

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is the British motoring organisation
then means at that time, formerly

explanation.surface: A former Olympic athlete belonged to a motoring club.
explanation.walkthrough: Olympian suggests an athlete, but means a god of Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of wisdom was one of the gods who lived on Mount Olympus.

indicators.note: the detective's name is placed inside the word for maturity

parts.note: age means maturity, being old enough
Vera is the TV detective DCI Vera Stanhope, of the British series Vera

explanation.surface: A detective grows nasty as she gets older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' reads as nasty, but is the arithmetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics the arithmetic mean is the ordinary average of values.

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An accusation drives Peter into a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Charge looks like an accusation, but means someone in one's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A person under another's patronage or guidance is their charge or ward.

parts.note: per means for each, for every
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: There is one for every lad.
explanation.definitionFit: One can mean an individual human, as in 'one must eat'.

definitions.meaning: leftover bits of food, as fed to animals

explanation.surface: People squabble over leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal scuffles are one sense; leftover morsels of a meal are the other.

clue.text: Length of time in a resort

indicators.note: time is placed inside the word for a resort

parts.note: a centre, like a holiday centre, is a resort people go to

explanation.surface: The length of a stay at a holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: This metric unit is a hundredth of a metre, a measure of length.

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers; the 's is read as 'has'
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A soldier's morale is low while serving in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: spirit looks like morale, but means a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlocked West African republic lies in Africa, hence a place there.

parts.note: L is a learner, as on British L-plates
to have dined is to have eaten

explanation.surface: A trainee had a meal and then left.
explanation.walkthrough: departed looks like 'left' but means dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are euphemisms for someone who has died.

parts.note: to pop is to go off with a bang

explanation.surface: An English bishop departs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bishop of Rome heads the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: British invader is no good when soused in drink

indicators.note: soused means steeped, so the no-good letters are steeped in the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A useless invader of Britain is drunk on beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angles were a Germanic tribe that invaded Britain in the fifth century.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Germanic tribe that invaded and settled England after the Romans.

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A defender in a match scores a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Defender reads as a sports position, but means one who argues a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues in support of a contested cause or belief defends it.

clue.text: Emphasised the sweet courses, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: desserts are the sweet courses of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone thinks back and insists on the puddings.
explanation.definitionFit: To put weight or accent on something is to give it emphasis.

clue.text: Mountain trail heading west in Asia

parts.note: Ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means read right to left

parts.note: to trail is to lag behind

explanation.surface: A mountain path leads westward through Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: trail looks like a path, but is the verb meaning to fall behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The region on the Bay of Bengal is split between India and Bangladesh in South Asia.
